extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, compliance officers, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Federal regulatory standards (34 CFR part 106) that recipients of Federal financial assistance must follow to prevent and respond to sex discrimination in education programs and activities, including definitions, notice/training/recordkeeping requirements, grievance procedures, and specific protections for pregnancy and parenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parental status (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parental status means the status of a person who, with respect to another person who is under age 18 or who is 18 or older but incapable of self-care because of a physical or mental disability, is: (1) a biological parent; (2) an adoptive parent; (3) a foster parent; (4) a stepparent; (5) a legal custodian or guardian; (6) in loco parentis; or (7) actively seeking legal custody, guardianship, visitation, or adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in applying nondiscrimination rules in admissions and other contexts; enumerates categories of persons covered as 'parental' for protections and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Party (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Party means a complainant or respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used throughout grievance and procedural provisions to identify roles in investigations and hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer retaliation (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer retaliation means retaliation by a student against another student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that retaliation protections cover student-on-student acts as well as actions by the institution or employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postsecondary institution (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Postsecondary institution means an institution of graduate higher education, undergraduate higher education, professional education, or vocational education that serves postsecondary students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the category of institutions to which certain subparts and obligations apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy or related conditions (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pregnancy or related conditions means: (1) pregnancy, childbirth, termination of pregnancy, or lactation; (2) medical conditions related to pregnancy, childbirth, termination of pregnancy, or lactation; and (3) recovery from pregnancy, childbirth, termination of pregnancy, lactation, or related medical conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the scope of pregnancy-related protections (used for nondiscrimination, reasonable modifications, leaves, lactation accommodations, and comparable treatment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program or activity / program (definition of coverage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program or activity means all operations of: (1) state/local governmental departments/agencies/instrumentalities receiving assistance; (2) colleges, universities, postsecondary institutions, public systems of higher education, local educational agencies, vocational systems, and other school systems; (3) entire corporations/partnerships/private organizations or comparable facilities to which Federal financial assistance is extended, including entities principally engaged in education, health care, housing, social services, or parks and recreation; and (4) any other entity established by two or more such entities, any part of which is extended Federal financial assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the broad, programmatic scope of Title IX coverage — recipients must consider all operations and subunits to which federal assistance is extended when applying nondiscrimination obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient means any State or political subdivision, instrumentality of a State or political subdivision, public or private agency, institution, organization, other entity, or person to whom Federal financial assistance is extended directly or through another recipient and which operates an education program or activity receiving such assistance, including any subunit, successor, assignee, or transferee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies who is legally obligated to comply with the regulations and to implement the stated policies and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant (evidence/questions) (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant means related to allegations of sex discrimination under investigation as part of the grievance procedures; questions are relevant when they seek evidence that may aid in showing whether alleged sex discrimination occurred, and evidence is relevant when it may aid a decisionmaker in determining whether alleged sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides evidentiary determinations in grievance processes and training on the meaning and application of relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedies means measures provided, as appropriate, to a complainant or any other person the recipient identifies as having had their equal access limited or denied by sex discrimination, to restore or preserve that person's access to the recipient's education program or activity after a determination that sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that remedies are corrective/restorative, tied to an institutional finding of discrimination, and directed at restoring access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent means a person who is alleged to have violated the recipient's prohibition on sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the role and rights of the accused party within grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retaliation (definition and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Retaliation means intimidation, threats, coercion, or discrimination against any person by the recipient, a student, or an employee or other person authorized by the recipient to provide aid, benefit, or service, for the purpose of interfering with any right secured by Title IX or because the person has reported information, made a complaint, testified, assisted, participated, or refused to participate in any investigation, proceeding, hearing, informal resolution, or other action under this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits retaliation broadly (by institution, students, or authorized persons). Notes that nothing precludes requiring employees or authorized persons to participate as witnesses or assist in investigations (i.e., compelled participation as witness is permitted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing authority (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing authority means that component of the Department delegated authority by the Secretary to appoint, and to review the decisions of, administrative law judges in cases arising under this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the Departmental component with appellate or review authority over ALJ decisions under these regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary school (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondary school means secondary school as defined by section 8101 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, and an institution of vocational education that serves secondary school students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to define coverage and obligations for K–12 recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex-based harassment (overall definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sex-based harassment, prohibited by this part, is a form of sex discrimination and means sexual harassment and other harassment on the basis of sex, including bases described in §106.10, and includes (1) quid pro quo harassment; (2) hostile environment harassment; and (3) specific offenses (sexual assault, dating violence, domestic violence, stalking).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames sex-based harassment as encompassing multiple categories that trigger different analyses and procedural responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quid pro quo harassment (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee, agent, or other person authorized by the recipient to provide an aid, benefit, or service explicitly or impliedly conditions provision of such aid/benefit/service on a person's participation in unwelcome sexual conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classic supervisor/authority-based harassment standard — grounds for immediate corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hostile environment harassment (definition and factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unwelcome sex-based conduct that, based on the totality of the circumstances, is subjectively and objectively offensive and is so severe or pervasive that it limits or denies a person's ability to participate in or benefit from the recipient's education program or activity (i.e., creates a hostile environment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a hostile environment exists is fact-specific and includes consideration of: (i) degree to which conduct affected complainant's access; (ii) type, frequency, and duration of conduct; (iii) parties' ages, roles, prior interactions and other relevant factors; (iv) location/context of conduct; and (v) other sex-based harassment in the program or activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific offenses (sexual assault, dating violence, domestic violence, stalking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified offenses are included as sex-based harassment: (i) Sexual assault — offense classified as forcible or nonforcible sex offense under FBI UCR; (ii) Dating violence — violence by a person who is or has been in a social relationship of romantic/intimate nature (relationship determined by length, type, frequency of interaction); (iii) Domestic violence — felony or misdemeanor crimes by a current/former spouse/intimate partner or person similarly situated, cohabitating or who shared a child, or acts against a victim protected under local family/domestic violence laws; (iv) Stalking — course of conduct directed at a specific person that would cause a reasonable person to fear for safety or suffer substantial emotional distress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides categorical examples of criminal conduct that are treated as sex-based harassment under the regulations and factors for relationship-based determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note on consent definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assistant Secretary will not require a recipient to adopt a particular definition of consent where that term is applicable with respect to sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients retain discretion to define consent in their policies; the Department will not mandate a single definition in all recipients' policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Student means a person who has gained admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies who is covered as a student for protections and procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student with a disability (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Student with a disability means a student who is an individual with a disability as defined in the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 or a child with a disability as defined in the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals interplay between Title IX obligations and IDEA/Section 504 protections; triggers consultation requirements in grievance implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures (definition and purposes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures means individualized measures offered as appropriate, reasonably available, without unreasonably burdening a complainant or respondent, not for punitive or disciplinary reasons, and without fee or charge, to: (1) restore or preserve access to the education program or activity (including safety measures); or (2) provide support during grievance procedures or informal resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets boundaries: supportive measures are non-punitive, individualized, and available to both complainants and respondents to preserve access and safety pending or during resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of State/local law and FERPA
rubrics_metrics.description: The obligation to comply with Title IX and this part is not obviated or alleviated by any State or local law or other requirement that conflicts with Title IX or by FERPA or its implementing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions cannot use conflicting state/local laws or FERPA as a justification to avoid Title IX obligations; must reconcile compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Title IX Coordinator (requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each recipient must designate and authorize at least one employee as Title IX Coordinator to coordinate efforts to comply with Title IX and this part; if more than one coordinator, one must retain ultimate oversight; delegation of specific duties to designees is permitted as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a named responsible official with coordination authority and requires clarity about ultimate oversight when multiple coordinators exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption, publication, and implementation of nondiscrimination policy and grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Each recipient must adopt, publish, and implement a policy stating it does not discriminate on the basis of sex and must adopt, publish, and implement grievance procedures consistent with §106.45 (and §106.46 if applicable) that provide for the prompt and equitable resolution of complaints alleging conduct prohibited by Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates written nondiscrimination policy and grievance procedures, publicly available and consistent with required grievance-process standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of nondiscrimination (contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide a notice of nondiscrimination to students, parents/guardians of K–12 students, employees, applicants, and unions/organizations. The notice must include: (A) a statement that the recipient does not discriminate on the basis of sex; (B) statement that inquiries may be referred to the Title IX Coordinator, OCR, or both; (C) name/title, office address, email, and phone number of the Title IX Coordinator; (D) how to locate the nondiscrimination policy and grievance procedures; and (E) how to report conduct that may constitute sex discrimination and how to make a complaint under this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must be prominent and include specific contact and procedural information; recipients may include information about exceptions or exemptions if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of nondiscrimination (publication requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must prominently include all notice elements on their website and in each handbook, catalog, announcement, bulletin, and application form available to persons entitled to notice, or used in recruitment. If format/size prevents full inclusion, recipients may include a shorter statement and provide the location of the full notice on the website. Recipients must not publish statements saying they treat applicants/students/employees differently on basis of sex except as permitted by Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires visible and accessible dissemination of nondiscrimination notice across common institutional publications and recruitment materials; allows limited alternative placement only when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training (general requirement and prohibition on sex stereotypes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must ensure designated persons receive training related to their Title IX duties promptly upon hiring or change of position and annually thereafter. This training must not rely on sex stereotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets frequency (initial + annual) and a substantive constraint (no reliance on sex stereotypes) on training content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for all employees (topics)
rubrics_metrics.description: All employees must be trained on: (i) the recipient's obligation to address sex discrimination; (ii) the scope of conduct that constitutes sex discrimination under Title IX and this part, including the definition of sex-based harassment; and (iii) applicable notification and information requirements under §§106.40(b)(2) and 106.44.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baseline training topics to ensure broad staff awareness of obligations, scope, and reporting/notification duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for investigators, decisionmakers, and implementers (topics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators, decisionmakers, and persons responsible for implementing grievance procedures or modifying/terminating supportive measures must be trained on: (i) obligations under §106.44; (ii) grievance procedures under §106.45 and §106.46 if applicable; (iii) how to serve impartially, including avoiding prejudgment, conflicts of interest, and bias; and (iv) the meaning/application of 'relevant' and types of impermissible evidence under §106.45 and §106.46 if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets due-process, impartiality, evaluation of relevance, and forbidden evidence for those conducting factfinding and determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for informal resolution facilitators (topics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilitators of informal resolution processes must be trained on the rules and practices associated with the recipient's informal resolution process and on how to serve impartially, including avoiding conflicts of interest and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures neutrality and process knowledge for those running informal resolutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for Title IX Coordinator and designees (topics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator and any designees must be trained on their specific responsibilities, the recipient's recordkeeping system and requirements, §106.44(f), and any other training necessary to coordinate compliance with Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinator-specific training duties include coordination, recordkeeping, and specialized procedural knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation for students with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: If complainant or respondent is an elementary or secondary student with a disability, the Title IX Coordinator must consult with appropriate members of the student's IEP team or placement decision group to determine how to comply with IDEA and Section 504 throughout implementation of grievance procedures. For postsecondary students with disabilities, the Coordinator may consult with designated disability support offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires cross-program coordination to ensure Title IX processes accommodate IDEA/Section 504 protections and services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping (7-year retention and contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must maintain for at least seven years: (1) records documenting each complaint's informal resolution or grievance procedures and outcomes; (2) records documenting actions taken in response to each notification received about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination; and (3) all materials used to provide training under the training provision — these training materials must be made available upon public request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies retention period and categories of records that support transparency, oversight, and future review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — protected characteristics included
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrimination on the basis of sex includes discrimination on the basis of sex stereotypes, sex characteristics, pregnancy or related conditions, sexual orientation, and gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that Title IX protections extend beyond binary sex to include orientation, gender identity, pregnancy, and stereotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application — programmatic reach (on- and off-campus conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: This part applies to every recipient and to all sex discrimination occurring under a recipient's education program or activity in the United States; conduct includes but is not limited to conduct in buildings owned/controlled by recognized student organizations and conduct subject to the recipient's disciplinary authority. Recipients have an obligation to address sex‑based hostile environments even when some alleged contributing conduct occurred outside the recipient's program or outside the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad territorial and contextual reach — schools must address hostile environments even with off-campus components if they affect access to the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissions — nondiscrimination generally
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall, on the basis of sex, be denied admission or be subjected to discrimination in admission by any recipient to which subpart applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms equal treatment in admissions decisions and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissions — parental/family/marital status and pregnancy
rubrics_metrics.description: In admissions, recipients must treat pregnancy or related conditions the same as any other temporary medical conditions; must not adopt policies concerning parental/family/marital status that treat persons differently on basis of sex; must not discriminate on basis of pregnancy or related conditions; and must not make pre-admission inquiries about marital status (e.g., 'Miss or Mrs.'). A recipient may ask an applicant to self-identify sex only if asked of all applicants and not used as a basis for prohibited discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets specific prohibitions on admission inquiries and mandates parity for pregnancy-related conditions in admissions decisions and policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education programs/activities — prohibition on exclusion and de minimis harm standard for sex-based separations
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided elsewhere, no person shall, on the basis of sex, be excluded from participation in, denied benefits of, or otherwise be subjected to discrimination under any academic, extracurricular, research, occupational training, or other education program or activity operated by a recipient that receives Federal financial assistance. Where Title IX permits different treatment or separation on basis of sex, such treatment must not subject a person to more than de minimis harm (except as permitted by statute/regulation). Adopting a policy preventing participation consistent with a person's gender identity subjects a person to more than de minimis harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits discriminatory exclusion and limits permissible sex-based separations to those that do not impose more than de minimis harm; explicitly protects gender identity-based participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy — responsibility to provide Coordinator contact when informed
rubrics_metrics.description: When a student or person with legal right acting on behalf of the student informs any employee of the student's pregnancy or related conditions, unless the employee reasonably believes the Title IX Coordinator has been notified, the employee must promptly provide the Title IX Coordinator's contact information and inform that person that the Coordinator can coordinate actions to prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an employee duty to connect pregnant students with the Coordinator and services unless Coordinator is already informed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy — reasonable modifications (individualized and consultative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must make reasonable modifications to policies, practices, or procedures as necessary to prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access; each reasonable modification must be based on the student's individualized needs and the recipient must consult with the student. A modification that would fundamentally alter the program is not reasonable. The student may accept or decline offered modifications; if accepted, the recipient must implement it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires case-by-case accommodations for pregnancy-related needs, consultation with the student, and a 'fundamental alteration' limitation; provides student autonomy to accept/decline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy — examples of reasonable modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonable modifications may include breaks during class to express breast milk, breastfeed, or attend to health needs; intermittent absences for medical appointments; access to online/homebound education; schedule or course-sequence changes; extensions of time for coursework and rescheduling of tests/exams; allowing a student to sit/stand or keep water nearby; counseling; changes in physical space or supplies (e.g., larger desk, footrest); elevator access; or other policy/practice changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-exhaustive list illustrating typical accommodations institutions may need to offer for pregnancy-related conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy — voluntary access to separate and comparable portions of program
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must allow a student to voluntarily access a separate portion of its program or activity provided the separate portion is comparable to that offered to students who are not pregnant and do not have related conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits voluntary separate programming only if comparable in quality and access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy — voluntary leaves of absence and reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must allow students to voluntarily take a leave of absence for at least the period deemed medically necessary by the student's licensed healthcare provider; if a recipient's leave policy allows a greater period, the recipient must permit leave under that policy if the student chooses. Upon return, the student must be reinstated to the academic status and, as practicable, extracurricular status held when leave began.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guarantees medically necessary leave and reinstatement protections; allows use of more generous institutional policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy — lactation space standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must ensure the student can access a lactation space other than a bathroom that is clean, shielded from view, free from intrusion, and may be used for expressing breast milk or breastfeeding as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets minimum facility standard for lactation accommodations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy — limitation on requiring supporting documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must not require supporting documentation for reasonable modifications, voluntary leaves, lactation space, or similar measures unless the documentation is necessary and reasonable to determine the modifications to make or whether to take additional actions. Examples when documentation is not necessary include obvious needs (e.g., larger uniform), previously provided documentation, or routine accommodations like allowing water or permitting breaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits burdensome documentation requirements and provides examples of when documentation would be unnecessary or unreasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy — comparable treatment to other temporary medical conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent consistent with pregnancy-specific requirements, recipients must treat pregnancy or related conditions in the same manner and under the same policies as any other temporary medical conditions with respect to any medical or hospital benefit, service, plan, or policy the recipient administers, operates, offers, or participates in for students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates parity between pregnancy-related conditions and other temporary medical conditions in benefits and policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy — certification to participate (limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must not require a student who is pregnant or has related conditions to provide certification from a healthcare provider that the student is physically able to participate in a class or activity unless: (i) the certified level of physical ability is necessary for participation; (ii) the recipient requires such certification of all students participating in that class or activity; and (iii) the information obtained is not used as a basis for prohibited discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restricts medical certification requirements so they apply only when genuinely necessary and nondiscriminatory in use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient response — prompt and effective response requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient with knowledge of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination in its education program or activity must respond promptly and effectively and must comply with the requirements of §106.44 to address sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the baseline duty to act when the institution knows or reasonably should know of potentially discriminatory conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient response — monitoring and addressing barriers to reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must require its Title IX Coordinator to monitor the education program or activity for barriers to reporting information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination and take steps reasonably calculated to address such barriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactive obligation to identify and remedy structural or cultural impediments to reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient response — employee notification duties (K–12)
rubrics_metrics.description: An elementary or secondary school recipient must require all its employees who are not confidential employees to notify the Title IX Coordinator when the employee has information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: K–12 employees (except confidential employees) have a mandatory reporting duty to the Coordinator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient response — employee notification duties (other recipients)
rubrics_metrics.description: All other recipients must, at minimum, require: (i) any non-confidential employee who either has authority to institute corrective measures or responsibility for administrative leadership, teaching, or advising to notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination; and (ii) all other non-confidential employees to either notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have such information or provide contact information for the Coordinator and how to make a complaint to any person who reports such conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates tiered reporting duties by employee role and ensures that reporting routes or contact info are routinely provided to reporting parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient response — student-employee status determination
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution must reasonably determine and specify whether and under what circumstances a person who is both a student and an employee is subject to the notification requirements applicable to employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires clear institutional policy about reporting obligations for individuals who are both students and employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient response — exception when employee is personally subject
rubrics_metrics.description: The notification requirements for employees do not apply to an employee who has personally been subject to conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes that employees who are victims may be treated differently (i.e., not required to report as employees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employee requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must notify participants how to contact confidential employees (excluding employees who are confidential only in research contexts). Confidential employees must explain to any person who informs them of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination: (i) their confidential status and circumstances when they are not required to notify the Title IX Coordinator; (ii) how to contact the Title IX Coordinator and how to make a complaint; and (iii) that the Title IX Coordinator may be able to offer and coordinate supportive measures and initiate informal resolution or investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures clarity about confidentiality limits and options for reporting and receiving supportive measures when individuals speak with confidential resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public awareness events (limits on obligation to act)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a postsecondary institution's Title IX Coordinator is notified of information provided during a public awareness event on campus or online, the institution is not obligated to act in response unless the information indicates an imminent and serious threat to health or safety. However, the institution must use the information to inform prevention efforts, including tailored training when information indicates possible multiple incidents in a particular part of the program or location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows institutions to use event disclosures for prevention and training but does not require formal response absent imminent safety concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator duties upon notice
rubrics_metrics.description: When notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, the Title IX Coordinator must take actions to promptly and effectively end any sex discrimination, prevent its recurrence, and remedy its effects, including treating the complainant and respondent equitably and offering/coordinating supportive measures for the complainant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinator must ensure equitable treatment and deploy supportive measures and other actions to stop discrimination, prevent recurrence, and remedy harms; this is the core operational duty upon notice.
